punchline: The 14-inch drive makers listened to their customers so well that, in Christensen's words, they were held captive by them.
thirty_sec: In the 1970s, disk drive makers listened to their mainframe customers and gave them a bit more capacity every year. Then startups brought out an 8-inch drive that held less and suited minicomputers. Two-thirds of the 14-inch makers never entered that market. When Seagate's even smaller drive got no interest from minicomputer makers, it sold to desktop PCs instead. Christensen calls this disruption.
